content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to this and trying to set up a [product_no] using [product_name] [version_no]. When I attempt to connect via Tools > Options > Interface, I can't find my device listed. I'm using Windows 7 Home, and my device appears as "Unidentified Network" and "Public" in the Network Center. Based on the status lights, there seems to be some communication, but connection fails. I tried manually entering the IP address, subnet mask, and gateway from the device, but I still get the message "Cannot access IP Address ***.***.**.***". Any help would be appreciated!

You need to set a static IP on your computer. Go to Local Area Connections > Properties > Internet Protocol (TCP/IP) > Use the following IP address, and set an IP similar to the [product_name] device's IP. For example, device IP: 192.168.010.002 and PC IP: 192.168.010.003. Make sure the subnet mask is 255.255.255.0. This should resolve your connectivity issue.
Thank you! That helped me—it turns out you need to set a similar IP rather than a different one for the device and PC.

I ran into the same issue. I tried entering my laptop’s IP into the configuration, and it did not work. My laptop is a corporate machine on Windows 7 and I can't change my IP address. Is there a technical reference for which IP should go where? I also tried pinging the device IP with no success.

You can go to Control Panel > Network and Internet > Network and Sharing Center > Change Adapter Settings. Then, find the connection the device is using, right-click Properties, select Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4), and set a suitable IP like 192.168.010.003. On your device screen, set a similar IP, like 192.168.010.004. In [product_name] Comfort software, add the device's IP under the Ethernet tab. If this doesn't work, you may need to request access from your company.

Thanks! I managed to connect, but I still get 'Download PC --> [product_name] failed' when trying to transfer the project. I don't think this is covered in the user manual. My subnet mask was incorrect.
Have you entered the subnet mask for both your Local Connection and the [product_name] device, as well as in your software? Can you clarify what is incorrect about it?

Hello [user_name], If downloads from PC to [product_name] fail, it can often be due to a block in your program lacking an output connection. After a failed download, check the info window at the bottom of the software for a message explaining the issue. Let me know if you have more questions—happy to help!
I'm interested in purchasing a [product_no] startup kit. Can I connect directly from the PC to the device’s LAN using a simple network cable, or is a network server always required?
You can connect directly to the device using a standard Ethernet cable.

I had the same connectivity problem and resolved it by checking the device's display for its IP address—mine was 192.168.0.1 by default. Enter this address in the PLC, and when prompted, adjust the IP if needed in your software. That fixed it—enjoy!

Hi, first confirm your cable is working. Then open Network and Sharing Center, go to the properties of your Local Connection, select Internet Protocol IPv4 (TCP/IP), and in the advanced settings, set your PC IP manually (e.g., 192.168.0.200) with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.0. Your [product_name] device's IP should match the first three segments of your PC's IP (e.g., 192.168.0.*). Try to connect after these changes.

Hello, May I ask a question? I have a [product_no] from [company_name] and a laptop, but I can't get communication working over a crossover Ethernet cable (cat5). What steps should I follow for a direct connection to the device? I need your advice urgently. Thank you.

Please review the discussion above; the answers are provided throughout. Ensure the IP range matches and use a straight cable, not a crossover. If issues persist, share more details so we can assist. Regards,

analysis.insight_summary: Users frequently encounter challenges connecting their computers to [product_name] devices using [product_name] software and Ethernet, with particular confusion around IP address and subnet mask settings. Device detection and initial connection are problematic for newcomers, and troubleshooting steps are often spread across community advice rather than documentation. Manual network configuration is usually needed, which users find unintuitive.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward, well-documented guidance for setting up direct PC-to-[product_name] device connections over Ethernet. They want step-by-step instructions for network configuration and downloading projects, along with better diagnostic tools and troubleshooting tips built into the software.
